subject: [ACTION] Pin grace period policy + rollback play for Private VPC
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@eastsidebank.com>
Cc: ops-team@eastsidebank.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: [ACTION] Pin grace period policy + rollback play for Private VPC

Team / Jamie,

Following our ops review last week I put together a concise proposal for how we handle short-term "grace" pinning for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers and the corresponding rollback play. This is targeted at customers that need a small pin window for stability during maintenance while still allowing us to ship critical fixes. Please review and annotate the attached draft.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Grace window duration: 72 hours by default (customer-facing), configurable down to 24h for low-risk hotfixes.
- Pin semantics: customer can request a temporary pin of a minor version (patch-level) for up to the grace window; longer locks require an approved pin request and SOW change.
- Maintenance windows: standard scheduled windows are weekday 23:00-03:00 UTC or a mutually agreed 4-hour window; emergency windows allowed with 48h notice for Dedicated/Private customers when possible.
- Rollback triggers (automated + manual):
  - Error rate > 3x baseline for 15m in prod after rollout.
  - Regressions on redline prompt set (automated eval) exceeding threshold.
  - Critical customer SLA impact (latency or availability).
- Rollback cadence: canary -> fleet rollback within 30m after trigger confirmed; full rollback runbook in attached rollback_runbook.md.
- Communication: pre-window announcement 7 days ahead for major versions, 48 hours for minor ship; 1-week notice recommended by customers for larger changes.

Open questions for internal review:
1) Do we want 72h or 48h as the default grace window? Pros/cons in doc.
2) Do we allow pinning of quantized variants (q4/q5) or only full-fp/ctr variants?
3) Where do we record a temporary pin (UI -> model pin audit + ticket ID)? Proposed: create a "temporary pin" object in Console that auto-expires and logs HMAC.

Attachments: pin_policy_draft.pdf (policy draft), rollback_runbook.md (playbook with commands and NetOps steps). Also DAR link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2bPinPolicyDraft

Ask: please reply in 24h with comments. If no blocking feedback, I'll schedule a short sync with Eastside ops for Friday.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [ACTION] Pin grace period policy + rollback play for Private VPC

Kimberly — quick notes inline below. I like the structure; a few pragmatic tweaks from an ops/runtime POV.

On Wed, Oct 21, 2026 at 9:02 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> High-level proposal (summary):
> - Grace window duration: 72 hours by default (customer-facing), configurable down to 24h for low-risk hotfixes.

I suggest default = 48h, not 72h. 48h gives customers a meaningful buffer while keeping our carriage return window tight enough to not block rolling fixes. Recommend making 72h an opt-in length for regulated customers (e.g., financials).

> - Rollback cadence: canary -> fleet rollback within 30m after trigger confirmed; full rollback runbook in attached rollback_runbook.md.

For network-sensitive customers (on-prem with NAT and specific BGP routes), the rollback timeline is often longer. Add a "netops hold" flag for certain routes which extends the fleet rollback window to 2h and requires manual confirmation by NetOps. Document per-account overrides.

> Open questions for internal review:
> 1) Do we want 72h or 48h as the default grace window?

My vote: 48h default.

> 2) Do we allow pinning of quantized variants (q4/q5) or only full-fp/ctr variants?

Allow pinning of functionally-equivalent quantized variants but mark them as "best-effort" in the UI. Some customers care about exact reproducibility; provide a warning.

I'll add concrete NetOps steps to rollback_runbook.md (drain commands, BGP drain checklist). Happy to pair with Soojin to finalize.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@eastsidebank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@eastsidebank.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Pin grace period policy + rollback play for Private VPC

Hi Kimberly / team,

Thanks for the clear proposal and the docs. Eastside Ops reviewed the attachments and we are generally aligned. A few notes from our side: 
- We can accept a default 48h grace window (we'd prefer 72h for major releases but are OK with 48h for minor/patches).
- We request a formal "one-week pre-notice" for any maintenance that will require machine reboots or >5% capacity churn. That's a contractual ask for our production change board.
- We need the NetOps hold flag documented in the runbook; we have a couple of internal routes that require manual confirmation before rollback.

Attached: eastside_approval.pdf (signed cover note approving the policy with the above caveats). Please incorporate the NetOps hold and the 1-week notice into the final policy. Once updated we'll route to our change board and provide final sign-off.

Thanks — Jamie
Jamie Ortiz
Head of Platform Operations
Eastside Bank
